skill.name: byted-mediakit-shared
skill.description: Routes media requests to the appropriate MediaKit audio, editing, image, or video skill. Documents shared CLI setup, operating modes, input handling, and asynchronous task polling.
skill.summary: Route media workflows and shared MediaKit CLI operations.
skill.author: volcengine

security_audit.summary: Most alerts are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, Chinese text, and task identifiers. Several command blocks execute or update external software, while local media can be uploaded through cloud mode without explicit per-file consent.

remediation.issue: Cloud mode can upload local media without an explicit confirmation step.
remediation.suggestion: Require confirmation before each local file upload and identify the destination service.

remediation.issue: Installation and update examples execute an unpinned package with automatic confirmation.
remediation.suggestion: Pin a reviewed package version and remove automatic confirmation from installation examples.

remediation.issue: Command examples place variable values into shell commands without quoting guidance.
remediation.suggestion: Use structured argument arrays or require strict validation and shell quoting for every substituted value.

content.value_statement: Complex media requests require the correct MediaKit domain and command contract. This skill routes requests and explains shared CLI setup, modes, inputs, and task polling.
actual_capabilities: Routes requests to MediaKit audio, editing, image, or video skills.
Explains MediaKit CLI installation, initialization, diagnostics, and command discovery.
Documents local and cloud execution modes for media tools.
Describes local path handling and the CLI media upload adapter.
Provides the shared protocol for querying asynchronous cloud tasks.
Requires tool help, schemas, and references before parameter construction.
limitations: It does not define parameters for individual media tools.
It requires mediakit-cli and the appropriate domain skill.
Cloud processing depends on account access, configuration, and network availability.
Local feature support varies by tool and installed dependencies.

use_cases.title: Plan a Video Edit
use_cases.description: Select the editing skill and identify required inputs before processing existing footage.

use_cases.title: Prepare Batch Images
use_cases.description: Route resizing, compression, recognition, or image quality requests to the image workflow.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Media Automation
use_cases.description: Choose local or cloud execution and track asynchronous tasks across a production workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Media Domain
prompt_templates.prompt: I need to [goal] with [media type]. Identify the MediaKit domain skill and ask for missing information before processing.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner routing for one media task

prompt_templates.title: Inspect a Media Tool
prompt_templates.prompt: For [goal], load the correct domain skill. Inspect the selected tool help, schema, and reference, then summarize required inputs.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Local Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Process [input path] for [goal]. Prefer local mode, confirm tool support, validate parameters, and report the output location.
prompt_templates.scenario: Execute a supported local media task

prompt_templates.title: Manage a Cloud Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a MediaKit workflow for [inputs] and [deliverable]. Confirm uploads, execute validated commands, poll genuine task IDs, and summarize results.

output_examples.input: Remove background noise from an interview and prepare the audio for editing.
output_examples.output: Selected the audio domain. Required inputs are the source media, desired output format, and any voice preservation requirements.

output_examples.input: Enhance a local video in cloud mode and wait for completion.
output_examples.output: Cloud upload confirmation is required. After submission, the workflow polls the returned task identifier and reports the final media result.

output_examples.input: Resize a folder of product images while preserving quality.
output_examples.output: Selected the image domain. The next step is to inspect batch support, size constraints, output format, and local processing availability.

best_practices: State the media type, processing goal, and expected output before choosing a domain.
Inspect current help, schema, and reference documentation before constructing parameters.
Confirm cloud uploads and use only genuine task identifiers returned by MediaKit.
anti_patterns: Do not guess a tool when the user has not stated a processing goal.
Do not invent paths, URLs, task identifiers, enum values, or business parameters.
Do not assume local and cloud modes expose identical parameters or results.

faq.question: Does this skill edit media directly?
faq.answer: No. It routes requests and explains shared CLI behavior. Domain skills provide specific tools and parameters.

faq.question: Which media domains are supported?
faq.answer: It routes audio, video editing, image processing, and video understanding or enhancement workflows.

faq.question: Is MediaKit CLI required?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow requires mediakit-cli and may require local media dependencies.

faq.question: Can processing remain local?
faq.answer: Some tools support local mode. Check the selected domain skill, tool reference, help, and schema first.

faq.question: Can local files be uploaded?
faq.answer: Yes. The CLI adapter may upload local media in cloud mode, so confirm the destination and user consent.

faq.question: How are asynchronous tasks checked?
faq.answer: Use the shared query protocol with the genuine task identifier returned by a cloud operation.
